author: claude
title: Biodynamic Preparations in Fine Wine Terroir

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: More and more famous wineries say they use biodynamic farming. What does that actually mean?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Biodynamics is a type of organic farming that started with lectures by Rudolf Steiner in nineteen twenty-four. Like organic farming, it avoids chemical pesticides and fertilizers. But it adds some special practices.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The most famous are the biodynamic preparations. They're numbered. Preparation five hundred is cow manure, put inside a cow's horn and buried in the ground over the winter. In spring, it's mixed with water and sprayed on the soil in very small amounts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It is. Preparation five hundred and one uses ground quartz, also buried in a horn, and it's sprayed on the leaves. The idea is to support soil microbiology, the life of tiny organisms in the soil, and to strengthen the plant.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I've also heard about the moon.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, many biodynamic farmers follow a lunar calendar. They plan work like pruning or bottling according to the moon and planets.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Is there scientific proof that it works?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The evidence is limited, and some ideas are hard to test. But many growers say their soils become healthier because they pay such close attention to the vineyard. Whatever the reason, some of the world's most respected wines are made this way.
